title: Vali's Death, as Valmiki Tells It
subtitle: Why Rama shot from hiding: Vali's question and Rama's answer, both in the text
frame: 16:9 (1920x1080), action kept inside a centred 9:16 safe zone
arc: Kishkindha Kanda (CE) 4.5 to 4.25: the fire-witness friendship, the brothers' feud, the two duels, Tara's warning, the arrow, Vali's accusation and Rama's answer, Vali's last words, Tara's grief, the funeral and Sugriva's crowning
sargas_read: 4.5, 4.9 to 4.25 (every verse), 4.11.37; translations cross-checked against the Devanagari where the English page is garbled (4.18.56 names Hanuman but the speaker is Vali; 4.19.26-28 is a mis-pasted Mandodari passage and is not used)

lines: पराङ्मुखवधं कृत्वा को नु प्राप्तस्त्वया गुणः ।
opening_sloka.translit: parāṅmukhavadhaṃ kṛtvā ko nu prāptastvayā guṇaḥ, yadahaṃ yuddhasaṃrabdhastvatkṛte nidhanaṃ gataḥ
opening_sloka.en: What merit have you gained by striking one whose face was turned away? Because of you, I, absorbed in battle, have met my death.
opening_sloka.why: The whole video is the answer to this one question, asked by Vali himself in Valmiki's text.

retention.owner_note: Nov 22 2026: the audio must be engaging so viewers don't leave midway.
plan: 0:00-0:15 cold open: the arrow, then Vali's question as a quote card; promise: 'Valmiki records Vali's accusation AND Rama's answer. By the end you will have heard both, word for word.'
Every beat ends on an open question that the next beat answers (the 'link' lines are recorded separately so reels can drop them).
Show the payoff early, explain it later: the two garlands are planted in act 1 and paid off in act 4.
Pattern breaks every 60-90 s: a quote card, a character's own line, a surprising detail (the year at the cave, the twins Rama could not tell apart).
Chapters in the YouTube description so viewers can jump instead of leaving.
Music per act: one symphonic piece per act (orchestra with Indian colour), sharing one recurring theme; smooth crossfades; quiet under every verse; builds to the climax, never harsh
Narrator stays calm (series rule) but alive: short lines, [thoughtfully]/[serious] contrast, [pause] before each reveal; characters speak their own key lines.

acts.name: Act 1 · Two brothers
acts.music: Act 1 (two brothers): night-forest mystery; solo bansuri over a tanpura drone and soft low strings, a gentle harp ostinato; a quiet brotherhood theme on cello that will return at the end

beats.title: Cold open: the question
beats.summary: One arrow from behind the trees. Vali falls and asks: what merit did you gain by striking one whose face was turned away? Promise both sides, word for word.
beats.link_out: But to answer him, we have to go back to a cave, and a year of waiting.

beats.title: The cave and the year
beats.summary: Sugriva's account: the demon Mayavi challenges Vali at night; the brothers chase him into a cave; Vali makes Sugriva swear by his feet to wait at the mouth; a full year passes; foaming blood flows out, demons roar, Sugriva hears what sounds like his brother crying out, seals the cave with a rock; the ministers crown him.
beats.link_out: And then the dead brother walked back into Kishkindha.

beats.title: The same stone, Vali's way
beats.summary: Sugriva offers the kingdom back with folded hands (4.10.4); Vali tells the court his version: he called 'Sugriva!' again and again, kicked the rock open, and found the door shut on him (4.10.17-4.10.20). He exiles Sugriva with one garment and takes his wife Ruma (4.10.21-22). Sugriva hides on Rishyamuka, where Vali cannot go (4.10.23).
beats.link_out: A brother with nothing left meets a prince who has lost everything too.

beats.title: A friendship sworn by fire
beats.summary: Hanuman brings Rama and Sugriva together; 'let hand be grasped by hand'; Hanuman kindles fire from two sticks and the two walk around it.
beats.link_out: Sugriva has one doubt: can anyone stand before Vali?

beats.title: Seven sala trees, one arrow
beats.summary: Rama's single arrow pierces seven sala trees, the mountain and the earth, and returns to the quiver. Sugriva falls at his feet: kill Vali today.
beats.link_out: So the first duel should have been easy. It wasn't.

acts.name: Act 2 · Two duels, two garlands
acts.music: Act 2 (two duels, two garlands): the theme grows; strings and soft horns build in long swells, light tabla and timpani rolls (never hard hits) for the duels; hushes for Tara's warning with a tender oboe/sarangi line

beats.title: The first duel: two brothers, one face
beats.summary: Sugriva roars, Vali bursts out; Rama, bow drawn, cannot tell them apart and does not shoot (4.12.20); Sugriva flees bleeding to Rishyamuka and accuses Rama (4.12.26). Rama: 'by voice, radiance, gaze, prowess and words I see no difference between you' (4.12.31).

beats.title: Two garlands
beats.summary: Lakshmana uproots a flowering gajapushpi creeper and puts it round Sugriva's neck so Rama can tell him apart. Vali already wears a garland: the golden one given by his father Indra. Plant: remember that golden garland.
beats.link_out: Back at Kishkindha, one person guesses the trap.

beats.title: Tara's warning
beats.summary: Tara holds Vali back: a beaten brother does not come back roaring without a strong ally; she has heard from Angada that it is Rama; make Sugriva crown prince, give up the feud.
beats.link_out: Vali's reply is the most painful line in the episode.

beats.title: 'How could he do wrong?'
beats.summary: Vali: 'Rama knows dharma and is grateful; how could he do a sinful thing?' (4.16.5). He swears Tara back by his life. She walks around him, prays for his victory, and goes in.
beats.link_out: Minutes later he was proved wrong, or was he?

beats.title: The arrow
beats.summary: The second duel; Sugriva weakens; Rama's arrow strikes Vali's chest. He falls like Indra's banner. Indra's golden garland holds his life, strength and splendour (4.17.5), so he lives long enough to speak.
beats.link_out: And what he said, Valmiki kept every word of.

acts.name: Act 3 · The question and the answer
acts.music: Act 3 (the question and the answer): almost still; sustained strings and a low choir pad, sparse harp notes; nearly silent under every quote and verse so the words carry

beats.title: Vali's accusation
beats.summary: Vali's speech, his own words: what merit in striking one whose face was turned away (13); I was fighting another (17, 21); I never harmed your land (20); if you had fought me openly you would have met Yama (39); like a sleeping man bitten by a snake (40); I would have dragged Ravana to you by the neck and found Sita (41-42); Sugriva taking the kingdom is right, but I was killed by adharma (43).
beats.link_out: Now Rama answers. This is the part most retellings shorten.

beats.title: Rama's answer: the law
beats.summary: The land belongs to the Ikshvakus and Bharata rules it by dharma; we carry out his law (6-11). An elder brother is like a father, a younger brother like a son (13-14). The reason: you live with your brother's wife Ruma while he lives (18-20); for this the punishment is death (22). And I gave Sugriva my word (27).
beats.link_out: But that still leaves the hiding.

beats.title: Rama's answer: why from hiding
beats.summary: Rama's own words: men catch animals with nets and traps, hidden or visible, fleeing or still; royal sages hunt; 'you are a shakhamriga (tree-dwelling animal), so fighting or not fighting, you were struck by my arrow.' Present it as the text gives it, no verdict.
beats.link_out: And then Vali did something no one expects.

beats.title: Vali folds his hands
beats.summary: Vali, hands folded: 'what you say is so' (41); forgive my harsh words (42). He does not grieve for himself or Tara as much as for Angada (46-47); asks Rama to treat Sugriva and Angada like Bharata and Lakshmana (49), and to see that Sugriva does not slight Tara (50).

acts.name: Act 4 · The goodbye
acts.music: Act 4 (the goodbye): grief and grace; the brotherhood theme returns on solo cello and bansuri, full warm strings swell as the golden garland changes hands, then settle into a peaceful major-key resolve with the rains

beats.title: Tara on the battlefield
beats.summary: Monkeys flee; Tara runs the other way: 'what is a son, a kingdom, my own life to me now?' She holds him: 'rise, kings do not sleep on the ground'; 'you would not hear my advice' (4.20.12).
beats.link_out: With his last breaths, Vali speaks to the brother he exiled.

beats.title: The golden garland changes hands
beats.summary: To Sugriva: we were not fated to be happy together (4); take the kingdom (5); protect Angada (8-10); 'Tara's judgement is never wrong' (14); do Rama's work (15); wear this golden garland, its fortune would leave it when I die (16). Sugriva's joy turns to grief (17).
beats.link_out: And his last words were for his son.

beats.title: To Angada, then silence
beats.summary: Bear joy and sorrow, obey Sugriva, neither too familiar nor too distant (20-23); he dies (24). Tara: 'salute your father'; Angada clasps his feet: 'I am Angada'.

beats.title: The fire and the rains
beats.summary: Angada and Sugriva place him on the pyre; Rama, sharing Sugriva's grief, arranges the rites (4.24.44). Rama will not enter the city for fourteen years (4.25.9); Sugriva is crowned, Angada made crown prince; the rains begin.

beats.title: Outro: what the popular version says, and what Valmiki says
beats.summary: Tulsidas's lines (quote cards) beside Valmiki's; both told with devotion. Valmiki gives Vali the full accusation and Rama the full answer; the viewer decides. SUBSCRIBE.

popular_compare.source: Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, https://ramcharit.in/kishkindha-kand/ (verbatim; doha numbers as the page gives them)

tulsidas.line: मेली कंठ सुमन कै माला। पठवा पुनि बल देइ बिसाला।।

pairs.valmiki: 4.12.35-36 (Lakshmana puts a flowering gajapushpi creeper on Sugriva)

tulsidas.line: पुनि नाना बिधि भई लराई। बिटप ओट देखहिं रघुराई।।
सुनु पति जिन्हहि मिलेउ सुग्रीवा। ते द्वौ बंधु तेज बल सींवा।।

pairs.valmiki: 4.15.6-23 (much longer: she has it from Angada, advises making Sugriva crown prince)
pairs.note: both; Valmiki's is a full counsel

tulsidas.line: कह बालि सुनु भीरु प्रिय समदरसी रघुनाथ। जौं कदाचि मोहि मारहिं तौ पुनि होउँ सनाथ।।

pairs.note: Tulsidas: if he kills me I am blessed; Valmiki: he knows dharma, how could he do wrong

tulsidas.line: धर्म हेतु अवतरेहु गोसाई। मारेहु मोहि ब्याध की नाईं।।

pairs.note: Tulsidas: two lines; Valmiki: the full speech

tulsidas.line: अनुज बधू भगिनी सुत नारी। सुनु सठ कन्या सम ए चारी।।

pairs.note: same core reason; Valmiki adds the law of Bharata's kingdom and the hunting argument for the hiding

tulsidas.line: अचल करौं तनु राखहु प्राना। बालि कहा सुनु कृपानिधाना।।

pairs.valmiki: no offer in 4.17-4.22 (read in full); Vali asks Rama to protect Angada and Sugriva to protect Tara, and gives Sugriva the golden garland (4.22.16)
pairs.note: difference; absence claim covers 4.17-4.22, whole death scene

tulsidas.line: छिति जल पावक गगन समीरा। पंच रचित अति अधम सरीरा।।

pairs.valmiki: 4.21.1-11: Hanuman consoles Tara; Rama speaks of time and destiny to Sugriva (4.24.2-11)
pairs.note: Tulsidas: Rama teaches Tara; Valmiki: Hanuman consoles her

popular_compare.page_typo: the page prints 'कुद्दष्टि' (for कुदृष्टि) in the line after 'अनुज बधू'; we don't quote that line

youtube_description:
Vali was shot from behind the trees, and as he lay dying he asked Rama: "What merit did you gain by striking one whose face was turned away?" (Valmiki Ramayana 4.17.13). Valmiki records his full accusation, and Rama's full answer (4.18). Two brothers, one cave, two garlands, and Tara, whose judgement "never fails" (4.22.14). Every line cited from the Critical Edition, with Tulsidas's telling beside it. Which argument weighs most for you?
